about: A person's level and its stat points (docs/design/skills-v2.md §12.1-12.2 as the owner's order 88 changed it, D-178, D-181; src/people/9999975-level). The level IS the power ladder's level (data/power.json levelCurve): one scale. A person is seeded at the level the ladder computes from his fighting worth, and from then rises only by defeating people and beasts, read on the same ladder, plus a floor for growing up. Experience is kept as the share of the way to the next level (0 to 1).

xp.about: Rising from level L to L+1 asks need(L) = e0 x growth^L x might(L) (might from the ladder, so each level asks more than the one before and the gap widens). One defeat of a foe of level F gives might(L) x rho for a stronger foe (rho = might(F) / might(L)), past upTo as upTo x (rho / upTo)^0.5, and might(L) x rho^weakPow for a weaker one; a foe gives nothing at all once you stand ceilAbove levels above it, and never lifts you past that line (no farming). Calibrated (the README): from 24, 20 defeats of soldiers (level 100) reach about 70, 80 reach about 110, and no number of them passes 125 (the owner's soldier, 75-125); from 100, 60 defeats of knights (175) reach about 165; from 225, 60 of a kingdom's best (340) about 295.

foes.about: Foes with no sheet of their own: a man killed in a battle or on a mission (a regular soldier on the ladder's anchors) and anyone else killed (an average grown person).

floor.about: Growing up: a person stands at least at floor(age) = grown x (age / the race's grown age)^pow, where grown = 24 + (mean potential - 42) / 3, held to 20..30 (the owner's average human 20-30). After the grown age only defeats raise the level.

points.about: Each level brings points (a race may set its own with GD.RACES[r].points), and one more at every bonusEvery-th level. A stat's ceiling is the person's potential x capMul (as A.train's); the body's room at an age is the ceiling x (roomChild + (1 - roomChild) x age / grown) below the grown age, the whole ceiling after; old age, wounds and illness lower what is read, not what is placed. A point costs 1 below half the ceiling, 2 to three quarters, 3 above. Placed points never move.

ways.about: The ways of life a household's or a post's placement leans to: two stats and who lives so. A career key of GD.CAREERS, or a post read from the person's offices, rank and occupation.
